There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

In a recent development, the three substantial guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Recent findings suggest that just like against Leeds at the weekend, Arsenal’s closing half hour was their best spell of the match. This was not their most fluent or creative performance, but sheer weight of pressure told and Lille cracked. The away team could not get out of their defensive third after half time, and after Timber’s goal the class of Saka, Havertz and Odegaard from the bench took over.

Two wins from two in the Champions League for Arsenal, joining Sporting and Barcelona as the teams with a 100 per cent record.

Just the three minutes of added time to play. Havertz has just been booked for catching the goalkeeper Ozer who was dallying on the ball.

Odegaard with a delightful first-time pass around the corner to Dowman, but the youngster cut inside looking for his goal and his shot was blocked. Maybe he could have looked for Saka across goal.

It has been revealed that arsenal happy to usher this game to a conclusion now. Dowman had one chance to run at the Lille defence from the right, but he played a pass expected a Havertz run that never came.

Industry observers note that max Dowman is now on for Eze. Saka will finish the game on the left, with Dowman on the right.

In a recent development, an extra treat for the Arsenal fans who have not made an early exit: Mikel Arteta is about to bring on Max Dowman. This feels like a presentable opportunity for a first Champions League goal, Lille have been non-existent in this half.

It has been revealed that the yellow card is coming out for Lille’s Goffi, who catches the inside of Eze’s ankle with his studs. The tackle did not quite have enough force to be worthy of a red card.

Bruno Guimaraes stings the palms of Ozer with a strike from the edge of the box, when perhaps he could have looked for Saka.

According to recent reports, olivier Giroud is on now for Lille, and he receives a standing ovation from most of the Emirates. A rarity when a former player returns.

Arteta has made another change: Ben White replaces Timber.

In a recent development, massive block by Ezri Konsa to help preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet, but Lille are still to have a shot on target. They were competitive in the first half, but have found the intensity too much too handle in the second 45 minutes.

That will answer some questions about his finishing, Arsenal’s No 7 rolls the ball into the bottom corner and they have scored three in seven second-half minutes. Slick combination play involving Timber, Odegaard and Havertz down the right, and the German played a cute ball back to Saka and he finished in style.

Arsenal have scored quite a few lovely team goals so far this season, including against Leeds United a few days ago. That was another one. The combination of Saka, Odegaard and Havertz was too much for Lille to handle. The arrival of those three substitutes has massively enhanced Arsenal’s attack.

Arsenal are on fire now 🔥 Bukayo Saka extends their lead to 3-0 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ZbCmhueaXo.

Eze goes close again with poked finish which the goalkeeper palms away from danger. Lille finished their league game with 10 at the weekend, and it looks like they legs have completely gone.

Bentaleb gives the ball away in midfield, and it is all too easy for Arsenal to find Saka in space down the right. He picks out Eze at the edge of the box, and his left-footed strike took a slight deflection and flew into the bottom corner.

It didn't take Arsenal long to double their lead ⚡️ Eberechi Eze scores to make it 2-0 🎯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/BVMieESgbi.

Here come the changes regardless: Saka, Havertz and Odegaard replace Madueke, Merino and Gyokeres.

Just as I say there is no space in the Lille box, Timber creates some with a superb first touch around the corner to his right before lifting the ball over the Lille goalkeeper Ozer. A finish worthy of any striker. Would it be harsh to say it’s the kind of finish Arsenal’s actual striker has never looked like providing?

In a recent development, arsenal have been working the ball into those positions inside the penalty box all game long, and finally it brings the breakthrough. There aren’t many defenders who can control and finish as cleanly as that, in a penalty box as crowded as it was there. A classy goal.

Recent findings suggest that this touch and finish from Jurriën Timber 😮‍💨 Arsenal lead against Lille! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/L2B6YsNDXo.

Odegaard and Saka are getting themselves ready on the bench, the changes are incoming.

Excellent recovery from Rice to snuff a Lille break, the ball just keeps coming back at the French side.

If anything, Arsenal have been almost too dominant. The game is a 10vs10 on the edge of the Lille box with no space.

It has been revealed that bruno Guimaraes has been Arsenal’s most enterprising player, and he has just gone down looking for a penalty. I think he was looking for it, and the on-field decision of no penalty stands. The defender may have trailed a leg, but it was unconvincing attempt from Guimaraes. Sam disagrees though!

I’m surprised that wasn’t given as a penalty. Looked like a clear movement into Bruno’s path, with no contact on the ball.

In a recent development, arsenal completely dominant now, without producing a final pass or shot of any great quality. Lille’s goalkeeper Ozer has not had to make a save in this spell despite all this possession. Lille penalised for taking too long over a throw, before Madueke’s shot is deflected through to Ozer.

Recent findings suggest that very obvious foul conceded by Gyokeres at the edge of the Lille box just as Arsenal were probing again. Then Bruno Guimaraes wins a free-kick in a crossing position left of centre. They are making hard work of it, but Arsenal do have Lille penned in.

Arsenal play a short one, and Timber is then flagged offside as Eze tries to find him with a reverse pass.

It has been revealed that bruno Guimarães loves a fist-pump to the home supporters and he’s produced a couple here tonight, in an attempt to lift the atmosphere. That’s not to say it’s a bad atmosphere but there is frustration building.

It took a long time for the referee to blow his whistle, but he gives a foul against Madueke on Perraud and Lille can clear their lines after a couple of minutes of Arsenal pressure.

It has been revealed that all Arsenal so far in the second half, and they work the ball well into Guimaraes at the edge of the area but he slices his shot wide with his weaker left foot. Feels like the home team are getting closer, though.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal with another Madueke corner, as they try to apply the pressure. Good delivery into the six-yard box, and it flicks off a Lille head for another corner on the far side. Rice to take.

Sources indicate that headed away. Clever Eze reverse pass to Timber, but crossing with his left foot is not his strong suit and he slices behind.

Arsenal win a corner inside 30 seconds of the second half after a Timber burst forward.

Slow starts have been a theme of late for Arsenal.

Arsenal haven't scored a first-half goal in any of their last five games in the Premier League or Champions League. Their last goal before the break was against Chelsea on 6 September. https://t.co/ZfScceDs6u.

The XI on the pitch are trusted to find the opening goal, and that also suggests Arteta is keen to manage minutes.

Barcelona are drawing at Galatasaray and Bayern Munich are 2-0 down against Viking. With Man City playing PSG tomorrow night, these are an notable three points for Arsenal to win, relative to the other teams we expect to fill the top spots of the league phase.

Absolute SCENES as Viking double their lead over Bayern Munich 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/rYqhAgwqyx.

According to recent reports, it has not been much of a spectacle so far, with Arsenal’s rotated attack stuttering but probably mustering enough chances to have scored by now. Lille managed one moment of danger with the offside goal, but are yet to have a shot on target. A half-time change by Arteta cannot be ruled out.

Great double save from Ozer in the Lille goal after Guimaraes’s shot from distance took a deflection, and he did well to get up and push the ball away from Gyokeres to deny the striker a tap-in.

Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer saves Bruno Guimarães' effort, then stops Viktor Gyökeres from tapping the ball in ⚡️ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/UYCmuevG22.

Andre heads Madueke’s corner behind for another one as half-time approaches. Good delivery to the near post this time but the Lille defence stands firm.

According to recent reports, eze with a loose square ball in midfield, but Arsenal are spared by an offside flag going up against Lille. Arsenal fans wanted the officials to play advantage with a break on.

According to recent reports, corner now for Arsenal. Lovely backheel from Madueke to Timber but his low cross towards Gyokeres is turned behind.

Arsenal yet to score from a corner this season.

Things look like happening for Arsenal when Guimaraes or Eze get on the ball around the top of the penalty area, accessing those areas has been the problem against a well-structured Lille team so far. Arsenal do not look unduly troubled but the home crowd would have expected more so far.

Mikel Arteta is becoming increasingly frustrated on the touchline, primarily with the officiating but one suspects he is also irritated by the wastefulness of his team. The Arsenal manager has, er, expressed some of these emotions to the fourth official, Richard Hempel. But Hempel, who appears to be an absolute German giant of a man, was having none of it. He really towers over Arteta and he wasn’t afraid to play that card.

Significant chance for Eze! But he shoots straight at the goalkeeper. The opportunity was created by a lovely defence-splitting pass from Guimaraes through the Lewis-Skelly, who dragged the ball back for Eze. The flag went up for offside, but Lewis-Skelly would have been onside.

It has been revealed that merino with a volley on the turn in the Lille box, but he slices over the bar. Snappy football from Arsenal and Rice to tee up Madueke for the initial cross.

In a recent development, then Arsenal work the ball patiently from right to left and Eze feeds Lewis-Skelly on the overlap, but his cross is too high and into the goalkeeper’s gloves. That needed to go along the six-yard line.

Sources indicate that eze caught offside after Lewis-Skelly did well to fizz a pass down the line into his feet. Arsenal’s first-choice attackers Odegaard, Saka and Havertz will not be fearing for their places at Forest on the basis of this first half.

Arsenal could do with a little more precision from their front three. Madueke, Eze and Gyokeres have had a few opportunities to hurt Lille but they haven’t done so yet. This is a big night for Eze and Gyokeres, especially, as they largely been marooned on the bench this season. With Tzolis out, Eze could lock down that left wing slot. But he needs to do more.

Another wasted Arsenal counter-attack, this time Merino turned the wrong way and misplaced a pass before making a frustrated challenge at the expense of a yellow card.

Arsenal probing, without really pulling Lille apart or unduly stressing their defence. Chance on a transition from a midfield giveaway, but Bentaleb did well to show Gyokeres wide and win the ball without conceding a free-kick.

According to recent reports, lille have the ball in Arsenal’s net but the flag goes up for offside! There was a double deflection from a Bentaleb shot, and the ball bounced off Haraldsson straight to Ueda, who finished past Raya from close range. The striker was onside when Bentaleb took his shot, but the second deflection did for him. There was a stoppage for a VAR check, but the decision stands.

As Sam remarked, the chances are starting to come for Arsenal now, with Timber lifting a cross straight on to the head of Merino but he failed to generate enough power and his effort was straight at the goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that madueke drops a shoulder to make room for a right-footed cross, but his delivery is over hit. Mikel Merino is playing in the Odegaard role tonight, but is not as nimble footed as the Arsenal captain.

That is Arsenal’s best chance so far though! Loose ball picked up and Timber released on the overlap, and it was a good pull-back to pick out Bruno Guimaraes but he fired wide.

There’s a goal coming here, and it’s going to be scored by Arsenal. They are finding gaps between the Lille lines and getting into some extremely dangerous positions in the inside channels. It feels like a matter of time.

David Raya gathers a cross after good defending from Timber, but then the Arsenal goalkeeper almost does a Shay Given against Dion Dublin at the edge of the box, but Rice put his foot in to get Raya out of bother. There was a frantic cry of “man on!” from the Arsenal crowd.

In a recent development, lewis-Skelly and Madueke both deliver crosses into the Lille penalty area but they are repelled. Arsenal lacking some familiarity with their combinations off the flanks so far, but Eze does well to burst past his man to tee up Guimaraes but the shot is blocked.

It has been revealed that arsenal fail to make the most of a wide free-kick, before Bruno G elicits a cheer from the crowd when he slides into a tackle at the expense of a throw in. With Lewis-Skelly at left-back and Eze in front of him, there is not much natural width on the Arsenal left.

Industry observers note that bentaleb, the former Spurs midfielder, puts his head up to pick out the stretching run of Ueda, but the Lille forward lacked support and the moved fizzled out. It’s been quite a tidy start from the French side.

From Czechia sub at Wembley last week, Ondrej Zmrzly, a man with no vowels in his surname, to tonight and Lille sub Soriba Diaoune who has the full set in his.

End-to-end football for a couple of minutes. Madueke with a cute reverse pass into Merino inside the box but it broke down for Arsenal, before Lille launched a dangerous counter-attack through on-loan Forest attacker Bakwa, who cut inside and let fly. Great block from Gabriel.

Madueke did some encouraging things against Leeds but has been a bit untidy so far, slipping and handling the ball before miscuing an attempted pass towards Timber on the overlap.

Then Lille do well to play out from deep and work the ball into midfield but Andre gives away a sloppy pass.

Both teams enjoying a feel of the ball in the opening exchanges, and there is some good work in a tight space down the right from Konsa and Timber but Madueke could not take the ball with him.

Arsenal then start to establish some dominance in the Lille half, moving the ball from side to side.

Lille get the game under way at the Emirates.

Declan Rice captains Arsenal. Were it not for Martin Zubimendi sustaining a knock in the post-Leeds warm down, Rice may well have been on the bench with Saka, Odegaard and Havertz.

Arsenal’s right-back has looked quite rusty on his fleeting appearances so far this season, searching for rhythm after a pretty serious groin problem. He pushed himself to appear in the Champions League final and subsequently missed the World Cup.

I would expect him to play like a third centre-back at times, allowing Lewis-Skelly to drift into midfield from left-back. That role might also help Timber preserve his legs.

It had escaped my attention that Arsenal defender Gabriel is facing his former club tonight. At £27m, signed in 2020, he has to go down as one of Arteta’s best signings, and one of the best value signings any Premier League club has made this decade.

According to recent reports, it’s very difficult. You come across very special people in life and Ken was certainly one of them. He’s an absolute legend of this football club. I think he’s the soul of this football club and someone that has given his life to this club.

This stadium wouldn’t be built if not for him. So, very sad news. The legacy he’s leaving is immense and our thoughts are with his family and we want to pay a proper tribute when we can.

Our players will be wearing black armbands this evening in memory of Ken Friar OBE. Rest in peace, Ken ❤️ https://t.co/xf91JABjrD.

Lille’s manager is Davide Ancelotti, the son of Carlo, and you would assume he has picked up a few tips and tricks from his dad about success in this competition. Carlo, after all, has won the European Cup on five separate occasions. This is Davide’s second job as a manager, following a spell at Brazilian side Botafogo.

Some of Bukayo Saka’s finishing has been wayward so far this season, but the volume of chances coming his way bodes well. At this fledgling stage of the season, only Erling Haaland is averaging more non-penalty expected goals per 90 minutes in the Premier League.

As Sam Dean explores in this piece, Arteta seems to be encouraging Saka to take up more central positions inside the box.

Sam writes: “Is Saka becoming a proper penalty-box predator? It is too early to say for certain but it is absolutely clear that he is taking up different positions, closer to the opponents’ goal, this season. Not only when the ball is on the left flank, but also when Arsenal are attacking through midfield.”.

Saka starts among the substitutes this evening, but will play his part towards the end of the game.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not problem Richardson with a caution.

In a recent development, lille noted the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

Recent findings suggest that “LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club noted. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”.

The artist Northbanksy has plumped for another Oasis-inspired dig at Manchester City, this time with Rui Pinto taking centre stage, the man whose leaked emails kicked off the Premier League investigation into City’s financial affairs.

A consequence of Piero Hincapie’s injury on Saturday (he hurt his ankle in a cool-down session after the game, embarrassingly) is that Myles Lewis-Skelly is seemingly now the backup left-back. Arsenal can’t trust Riccardo Calafiori’s body to play two games in a week and are clearly saving him for Premier League action on the weekend. Lewis-Skelly has been so impressive in midfield that it must be frustrating to change position now.

Bakwa is on loan from Nottingham Forest, while those at the Emirates with long memories will remember that Nabil Bentaleb played for Spurs. Only the knowledgeable shall boo.

Lille XI: Özer; Perraud, Alexsandro, Ngoy, Goffi; Bentaleb, André; Mukau, Haraldsson, Bakwa; Ueda.

Subs: Gill, Srdanovic, Giroud, Sahraoui, Kjaergaard, Onal, Kouassi, Verdonk, Cossier, Perrin, Diaoune, Sajous.

Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard drop to the bench, so some rotation from Arteta with a weekend trip to Nottingham Forest in mind, a venue where Arsenal have drawn 0-0 on their last two visits.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Bruno, Rice; Madueke, Merino, Eze; Gyokeres.

Subs: Meslier, Kepa, White, Mosquera, Salmon, O’Neill, Hashi, Saka, Odegaard, Havertz, Dowman.

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW.

Sources indicate that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

In a recent development, as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Sources indicate that lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

It has been revealed that leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

According to recent reports, arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:24, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:27.

Having left for the international break on a rare low, Como will aim to resume their stellar start to the season when Cagliari visit Stadio Sinigaglia on Saturday.

Not only are the Lariani making a significant impact in Europe, they have been breaking new ground in Serie A - but defeat to the champions recently slowed their charge towards the top four.

Como have caught the eye in this season's Champions League - notably following their famous 4-1 defeat of Manchester United with a ruthless 9-1 destruction of Lens - and they also have major ambitions in Serie A.

Remarkably, the European rookies sit above Barcelona and Bayern Munich in UEFA's top competition, and they had posted six straight wins across all competitions before facing Inter Milan last time out.

Overseen by one of football's most-wanted coaches, the Lariani scored 22 goals and conceded just four during that hot streak, but it came to an abrupt end at San Siro.

Como's 12th consecutive league defeat to Inter left Cesc Fabregas and co five points behind the Scudetto holders, while costing them their place in the top four.

As a manager, Fabregas has yet to conquer Inter in either Serie A or the Coppa Italia, but his team tend to take care of business against Italy's lesser lights.

Now heading back to base, Como have kept clean sheets in their last three league matches at the Sinigaglia, where they have never lost a top-flight clash against Cagliari.

Beaten 2-1 when the pair most recently met, Cagliari's last Serie A win over Como dates back to March 1982 - albeit both clubs have spent plenty of time outside the top tier.

This term, the Sardinian side will head to Lombardy full of confidence, as they sit just inside the top half following a largely positive start to the current campaign.

Hurtling out of the blocks, Fabio Pisacane's men claimed four victories from their opening five fixtures - only losing to Inter - before slipping back into the pack with a less successful run.

Yet, when facing down Frosinone after suffering four consecutive defeats, Cagliari came out on top: Michel Adopo's goal gave them a 1-0 win over the newly promoted high-flyers.

All told, a haul of 16 points from their first 11 matches represents the Rossoblu's best top-flight start since 2019, and Pisacane has been handed much of the credit.

Continuing an injury-hit start to his Como career, Moise Kean has suffered a setback in his recovery from a tibia problem and could be sidelined for several more weeks.

Wide men Jayden Addai and Jesus Rodriguez are also unavailable, but Fabregas hopes to have Assane Diao and Trevoh Chalobah back in the squad.

The hosts' star man, Nico Paz helped Argentina beat Costa Rica 7-0 earlier this week, scoring his first international brace.

In a recent development, the 22-year-old has already posted 14 goal involvements for Como this season, attracting interest from Europe's top clubs. Curiously, though, just two of his last 11 Serie A strikes have come on home soil.

While Paz should link up with Greece striker Tasos Douvikas in the final third, Cagliari's front line may be led by Paul Mendy and Daniel Maldini - the latter of whom has found the net five times this term.

Although Pisacane can recall Adam Obert after the left-back served a suspension against Frosinone, several men are still missing through injury.

Alieu Fadera and Mattia Felici have been ruled out, while M'Bala Nzola (flexor), Harry Winks (back) and Yerry Mina (thigh) are all struggling to return in time.

Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas.

Cagliari possible starting lineup:.

Caprile; Ze Pedro, Kofler, Rodriguez, Obert; Adopo, Romano, Deiola; Fazzini, Maldini; Mendy.

Free-flowing Como can score from all quarters, while Cagliari must head to the mainland on a run of three away defeats, in which they shipped 10 goals.

So, the hosts will resume winning ways after their setback in Milan, keeping them on the tails of Italy's top three.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Chelsea entered the international break with renewed questions to answer after a mixed run of results under Xabi Alonso.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon aiming to bounce back from a disappointing defeat before the international break when they host Leeds United in the Premier League.

The two clubs already served up an entertaining encounter earlier this season, with Chelsea coming from behind to secure a dramatic 6-3 victory in the EFL Cup. This latest meeting could prove equally important, as only two points separate the sides in the league table.

Chelsea entered the international break with renewed questions to answer after a mixed run of results under Xabi Alonso.

The Blues had recovered from a surprise home defeat to Tottenham Hotspur by beating Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, only to suffer a disappointing loss away to Sunderland in their final match before the break.

Alonso’s side have collected five wins, one draw and four defeats from their opening 10 Premier League fixtures, leaving them fifth in the table. While they remain firmly in the hunt for a top-four finish, the race is becoming increasingly congested, with just three points separating Chelsea from 10th-placed Aston Villa.

As veteran midfielder Jordan Henderson pointed out, consistency will be the key for the Blues’ prospects between now and the end of the season.

A return to Stamford Bridge should provide encouragement. Chelsea have accumulated 10 of their 16 league points at home and have scored 13 goals in front of their own supporters, the second-highest home tally in the division.

It has been revealed that the Blues also boast an impressive recent record against Leeds on home soil, winning eight of their last 10 meetings at Stamford Bridge across all competitions. However, they were held to a 2-2 draw in this fixture last season after surrendering a two-goal advantage.

Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Jamie Gittens remain unavailable through injury.

There is hope that Joao Pedro could return after missing the last four matches due to a thigh problem, while Moises Caicedo, Jorrel Hato and Josh Acheampong are all fitness doubts.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is expected to return after recovering from a broken jaw and representing Argentina during the international break.

Morgan Rogers was one of Chelsea’s standout performers in the EFL Cup victory over Leeds, providing four assists, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both scored twice. However, Welbeck may start on the bench, with Alonso potentially favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central attacking role.

Leeds arrive in West London in significantly better spirits after ending a difficult spell before the international break.

Daniel Farke’s side had gone five matches without a victory before recording an vital 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. Noah Okafor’s late strike secured all three points and lifted Leeds into ninth place, just two points behind Chelsea.

It has been revealed that the victory continued an encouraging home run, but Leeds have found life much tougher away from Elland Road. They have won only one of their last eight league fixtures on their travels, drawing four and losing three.

A demanding sequence of away matches now awaits, with trips to Chelsea, Manchester City, Liverpool and Aston Villa on the horizon.

Recent findings suggest that there are reasons for optimism, though. Leeds are unbeaten in their last two league meetings with Chelsea, following up a 3-1 home victory with a 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge. They now have the chance to go three consecutive league games without defeat against the Blues for the first time since 2001.

Speaking to the press ahead of the game, Farke was full of praise for the quality in Chelsea’s ranks.

Mateo Joseph continues to recover from a serious knee injury and remains unavailable.

Anton Stach is a doubt after missing the victory over Tottenham with a broken toe.

Farke could continue with a front two consisting of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, while Ethan Ampadu is expected to feature in midfield.

Noah Okafor will be pushing for a starting role after scoring from the bench against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are all contenders to return to the lineup.

Chelsea’s recent performances have lacked consistency, and the potential absence of a natural focal point in attack has reduced their threat in front of goal.

It has been revealed that leeds arrive with renewed confidence after their victory over Tottenham and have shown in recent meetings that they can cause problems for the Blues. However, their away form remains a concern, particularly against a Chelsea side that generally performs much better at Stamford Bridge.

It should be a close contest, but Chelsea’s superior attacking quality and strong home record give them the edge.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

In a recent development, 🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3.

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes.

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute.

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again.

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

  • Thomas Frank has provided his first injury update as Crystal Palace manager ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Coventry City at the CBS Arena.
  • Nine months after his sacking by Tottenham Hotspur, Frank was appointed the new Eagles boss on Monday, just five days after Pierre Sage was relieved of his duties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:35, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 18:36.

Thomas Frank has provided his first injury update as Crystal Palace manager ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Coventry City at the CBS Arena.

Nine months after his sacking by Tottenham Hotspur, Frank was appointed the new Eagles boss on Monday, just five days after Pierre Sage was relieved of his duties.

The Dane has taken over a Palace side that sits rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 top-flight fixtures, including a 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool before the international break.

Defender Takehiro Tomiyasu has been sidelined for the last nine matches in all competitions with a calf injury, while last season’s top scorer Ismaila Sarr has been limited to only 15 minutes of Premier League action this term due to an ongoing groin problem.

Speaking at a press conference on Thursday afternoon, Frank confirmed that both players will not be ready to return for the trip to Coventry.

"I can say that Tomiyasu will be back training next week," Frank told reporters. "On Sarr, it'll be touch and go when he can start training. It's a groin injury so you need to be careful.

Recent findings suggest that "You need to be aware with those injuries about how much you push. That could take a little longer time. You need to make sure that you don't take two steps forward, to then take two steps back.

"This could take a little longer. He'll not necessarily be on the pitch next week.".

Chadi Riad (knee) remains a long-term injury absentee for Palace, while there was no mention of Jorgen Strand Larsen at Frank’s press conference, but the striker has been spotted in training this week after withdrawing from the Norway squad with an ankle matter.

Meanwhile, striker Jean-Philippe Mateta will serve the second of a three-match suspension this weekend following his red card against Tottenham at the end of last month.

Palace are hoping for an immediate manager bounce under Frank following a disappointing run of four straight defeats in the Premier League.

The Eagles won their first four visits to the CBS Arena between 2005 and 2008, but are winless in their last four across all tournaments between 2009 and their most recent trip in 2012 (D2 L2).

Discussing the challenge of facing Coventry in his first game as Palace boss, Frank stated: "I know it'll be difficult.

Recent findings suggest that "But I also trust the boys, I know we'll perform on Saturday. We just need a little margin to go in our favour.".

Victory for Palace could see them climb off the foot of the table and out of the relegation zone up to as high as 16th place – above Coventry at the moment in 17th – if other results go their way this weekend.

Martin Zubimendi is seriously considering leaving Arsenal for the first time and has refused to rule out a move to Chelsea, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game for Arsenal this season, with the concerning lack of game-time sparking speculation over his future at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spanish midfielder enjoyed a bright start to his Gunners career following a £60m move from Real Sociedad, earning rave reviews from Mikel Arteta this time last year.

But Zubimendi had lost his place in the Arsenal team by the end of the season, with a teenage Myles Lewis-Skelly instead starting the Champions League final against PSG.

The 27-year-old has continued to struggle for minutes this season and is now, for the first time, considering his future at the club.

Spanish outlet AS say Zubimendi has his eye on a January exit and is ‘open to everything’ following reports linking him with Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid.

Xabi Alonso is keen to strengthen his midfield options and knows Zubimendi well from his previous spell at Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi is contracted to Arsenal until 2030 but reports in Spain say the north London club will consider offers for the World Cup winner of at least £60m.

Last week, Zubimendi was forced to address speculation linking him with a move away from Arsenal while on international duty with Spain.

Sources indicate that ‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too,’ he told Marca. ‘I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

In a recent development, ‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. Newly introduced signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

‘I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time. I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too. Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

‘I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very rapidly.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has broken two England Under-21 records previously held by Jude Bellingham in a matter of days.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to play for the Three Lions at Under-21 level when he came off the bench on Friday in a 1-0 defeat to Portugal.

Dowman then started against France at Aston Gate on Monday night, scoring a dramatic late winner in a 3-2 victory.

His appearance against Portugal broke Bellingham’s record as youngest England Under-21 player and his goal against France broke the Real Madrid superstar’s record as youngest to score at this level.

Dowman was 16 years and 320 days when he scored in Bristol on Monday, while Bellingham was 17 years and 67 days old when he made his debut against Kosovo in 2020, scoring on his first appearance for England Under-21s.

Also on the scoresheet for England in the friendly win over France were Tottenham’s Mikey Moore and Manchester City’s Divin Mubama, who is on loan at Southampton this season.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis captained Lee Carsley’s side, while the likes of Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood and Liverpool’s Trey Nyoni were also in the starting XI.

It was Dowman who was making yet more history, though, having already become the youngest player to score in the Premier League and to make an appearance in the Champions League.

When Arsenal won the title last season, he also became the youngest player to lift the Premier League trophy.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incredible talent does not turn 17 until December 31 and will hope to get more run outs for Arsenal before then, although he has only had one very brief substitute appearance for the Gunners since his red card against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on October 27.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was clearly fuming with Dowman when he was shown a straight red card for reacting to a heavy challenge against Fleetwood, giving the youngster stern words as he left the field.

Arteta mentioned: ‘I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘But, I don’t know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say “I don’t like the reaction”. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am.’.

In a recent development, he added: ‘The reaction when I don’t win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] massive time.

‘So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has vowed to give his “very best” to ensure that the Eagles will avoid relegation from the Premier League this season.
  • The 53-year-old was officially unveiled as Palace’s new boss on Monday, just five days after the sacking of his predecessor Pierre Sage who lasted less than five months at Selhurst Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:49.

New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has vowed to give his “very best” to ensure that the Eagles will avoid relegation from the Premier League this season.

The 53-year-old was officially unveiled as Palace’s new boss on Monday, just five days after the sacking of his predecessor Pierre Sage who lasted less than five months at Selhurst Park.

Frank has taken over an Eagles outfit that is sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 games and conceding a division-high 24 goals.

The Dane was believed to be on Palace’s radar in the summer, but he made it clear that he wanted an extended break away from management before assessing his options.

Frank now feels that the time is right to return to the Premier League “circus” for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February after a underwhelming eight-month spell in charge, winning just 34.2% of his 38 games in North London.

Remembered fondly for his successful seven-year tenure as Brentford boss, Frank is excited to take the reins at an “iconic” club in the form of Crystal Palace and is confident that he can steer them away from trouble.

It has been revealed that speaking at his first press conference on Thursday afternoon ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash at Coventry City, Frank told reporters: "It's good to be back! It's a little bit of surprise, the feeling I have in the body; how good it feels.

"Of course I said yes for a reason, to join Palace and go back into the circus and into the Premier League.

"It's just so good to be back and I'm in no doubt there won't be times where it won't feel like that, but I'm happy to be here.".

"For me Palace is an iconic club in England and it's also shown that, in many years in the Premier League, doing fantastic things,” Frank added.

"Selhurst Park is a fantastic place to go, to watch football, to feel the atmosphere, to feel a proper game.

Sources indicate that "I think Palace, when I've faced them over the years have always been a tough team to play. It's always been difficult.".

Frank was enjoying a break away from football in Australia with his family, but he was persuaded by Crystal Palace to return to the Premier League in the middle of a season.

It has been revealed that "It's been of course extremely busy. In every aspect, of course, to join a pre-season is a privilege and I've had the privilege to do that in the other clubs I've been in,” mentioned the Dane.

"The good thing is that you want to implement all your ideas, and that will take some time to hit the ground running, but I know what I want and the direction we should go in.

"Timing - in life and football - is everything. I was enjoying my life in Australia. It's pretty nice down there. Nice weather together with the family. And I'm a person that really enjoys football, it is my life. It's scary to feel how I feel, how it feels to be back.

"I'll speak to my good friend Roy [Hodgson] of course and speak to him - I don't want to go as long as he did - but it's good, that feeling. Good to be back.".

Commenting on improving results at Selhurst Park and moving away from the relegation zone, Frank added: "I'm looking forward to come in to do everything I can to help the team, the club.

Sources indicate that "I think it's a very talented squad. I think it's got good potential in every aspect.

"Of course we are in a position where we don't want to be, and I'll do my very best together with the staff and players to make sure we're in a much better position when the season is done.".

Crystal Palace, who have spent the last 14 years in the top flight, could climb out of the relegation zone if they end their four-match losing streak with a victory at Coventry this weekend and other results go their way.

Meanwhile, Frank has also provided a fresh injury patch on attacker Ismaila Sarr and defender Takehiro Tomiyasu ahead of their trip to the CBS Arena.

Jesus Owono’s punishment criticised following death of Jesus de Miguel

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andorra owner Gerard Pique notes Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.
  • The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was revealed that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.
  • Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andorra owner Gerard Pique notes Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was revealed that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.

It swiftly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the centre-forward’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated – and he died the following day.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the days and weeks that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Last week, Owono learned that he would be banned for Andorra’s next 12 matches for the role he played in the deadly collision, with the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee stating that the player had ‘violently struck an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

It went on: ‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

The statement added that the ‘nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances’ meant that the ‘maximum sanction’ was ‘justified’.

It was also confirmed that the match involving Andorra and Tenerife – which was called off when the teams were locked at 2-2 deep into stoppage time – would not be replayed.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred,’ it read.

Owono’s suspension has received a mixed reaction in Spain, with some feeling it too lenient while others have called for the ‘distressed’ goalkeeper to be given greater support.

According to Andorra owner Pique, the former Barcelona, Manchester United and Spain defender, Owono is ‘not to blame’ for the tragic outcome of the deadly collision.

‘I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve,’ he remarked in a statement.

‘He is not to blame for all of this having happened.’.

Pique pointed to a separate incident earlier this month in Spanish football, when Albacete attacker Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell’s Quadri Liameed in the head during a second-tier encounter.

‘Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,’ Pique added.

‘With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?’.

Pique, a World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, made it clear that Owono would likely require a significant break away from the game before being able to compete again.

‘Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to play,’ he continued.

‘No sanction is going to bring De Miguel back to us.’.

Tenerife’s grieving squad returned to action for the first time since De Miguel’s death against Cueta on Sunday.

Goals from Nacho Gil and Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife a 2-0 victory on an emotional day the club’s Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

Lisandro Martinez will also be free to return to the squad, having served a suspension against Villa, but it appears unlikely that Luke Shaw will be involved.

Benjamin Sesko, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are definitely out, while Marcus Rashford needs to be assessed due to a hip problem.

Pochettino will hold his pre-Liverpool press conference on Friday afternoon, where he will provide an update on the team's injury situation.

Recent findings suggest that "I think it's an opportunity," Pochettino told MUTV in his first interview. "It's a privilege to be, you know, head coach of Manchester United and I think we cannot waste time.

Sources indicate that "We need to be ready to compete [on] Sunday. Now it’s not time to think about rest, it’s not time to think about sleep. It’s about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.".

Mauricio Pochettino is having to squeeze a lot into his first days as Manchester United, but there will be time for one tried-and-tested tradition.

It has been revealed that the Argentine touched down in Manchester on Wednesday, just hours after overseeing USA’s 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati. The new head coach has conducted his first interview with club media, posed for photos and met the players.

On Thursday, Pochettino will take charge of his first training session at the club’s Carrington base before conducting his first press conference on Friday ahead of his first game on Sunday, which is a daunting trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool.

But there will see be time for a team dinner.

The Independent report that Pochettino plans on taking the players and staff out for a team bonding evening, and he will be picking up the tab.

Sources indicate that it is a tradition Pochettino is said to have first introduced the custom during his time at Southampton, believing it was an crucial way to build relationships and strengthen the bond within a squad. He then did it at Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

It has previously been reported elsewhere that Pochettino held team dinners a number of times during his five-and-a-half-year tenure at Spurs.

Recent findings suggest that with Pochettino taking charge midway through the campaign, there is no opportunity for a traditional pre-season or an extended period to get to know his players. The dinner will therefore provide an early chance for the 54-year-old and his coaching staff to assess the group's dynamics away from the training pitch.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino believes creating a strong sense of togetherness is essential to success, and the gathering will allow him to begin establishing his approach at Old Trafford. It will also give players and staff an opportunity to get to know their new manager and his backroom team in a more relaxed setting.

With a demanding schedule ahead, Pochettino will hope the occasion helps lay the foundations for a successful union between players and staff.

After a poor start to the season, United sit 18th in the Premier League with just one win in 10 games and are out of the Carabao Cup after a defeat at home to Brighton in September.

United’s players have been booed by supporters at Old Trafford but Neville believes Diogo Dalot has been made an ‘easy target’ and has defended the Portuguese full-back because of his work-rate.

Neville also feels Pochettino will look to move on Noussair Mazraoui, Matthijs de Ligt, Mason Mount, Marcus Rashford and Joshua Zirkzee at the end of the campaign, and expects Lisandro Martinez to leave when his contract expires next summer.

‘Do I think Dalot is Denis Irwin? No. Let’s be really clear, Denis Irwin is the greatest full-back Manchester United have ever had, I shouldn’t be mentioning him in the same breath, but I would get rid of a few before Dalot,’ Neville said on Stick to United.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night.

The new Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium.

He was greeted by kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow - members of the Bengals' special teams - on the turf before kickoff.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The game, which will take place around a mile north of the Bengals' Paycor Stadium, will mark Pochettino's final match in charge of the US national team.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Sources indicate that pochettino will begin his latest role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending fresh job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he mentioned. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Industry observers note that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

It has been revealed that ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

According to recent reports, ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:54.

Sunderland will endeavour to claim back-to-back Premier League victories and climb out of the relegation zone when they travel to Villa Park to face Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw across seven games in all competitions, Aston Villa have failed to come out on top in any of their last four matches (D2 L2), with their latest setback sparking a furious reaction from manager Unai Emery.

Villa allowed Man United to come from two goals behind twice and salvage a point in a chaotic 4-4 draw at Old Trafford prior to the international break, with the visitors conceding two goals in stoppage time to be denied what would have been just their third win at the Theatre of Dreams in 32 visits.

Three wins, four draws and three defeats have been posted by the Midlands club in 10 top-flight games this term, leaving them sitting 10th in the Premier League table and five points behind the top four where they finished last season.

Since the beginning of October, Villa have dropped a joint-division-high six points from winning positions, while their defensive concerns remain having conceded in 13 of their 16 matches across all competitions this season.

Heading into Emery’s 150th Premier League game in charge this weekend, Villa have found the net 14 times across a five-game unbeaten home run (W3 D2), while they have lost just one of their last 12 top-flight meetings with Sunderland (W5 D6) – a 3-1 away defeat in January 2016.

Sunderland ended a miserable seven-game winless run in the Premier League with a much-needed 1-0 triumph over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light before the international break, courtesy of a first-half penalty from Enzo Le Fee.

Head coach Regis Le Bris was delighted to see his Black Cats side ‘re-connect with our identity and our fans’ after delivering a gritty and disciplined display that helped them climb off the foot of the Premier League table for the first time in three weeks.

Now sitting 19th and only three points behind Hull in 13th spot, Sunderland will be looking to win consecutive top-flight games for the first time this season when they make the trip to Villa Park this weekend, as well as end their five-game winless streak on the road.

The Black Cats sit rock bottom of the away form table having accumulated only one point (D1 L4) and conceded a joint-division-high 13 goals, including three in a 3-1 defeat at Coventry City at the end of last month.

Sunderland now head to the Midlands seeking to end a seven-game winless run away against Aston Villa across all competitions (D3 L4), with their last victory at Villa Park coming in January 2011 when Phil Bardsley’s late strike secured a 1-0 Premier League triumph under Steve Bruce.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana – who signed a contract extension earlier this week – and Matteo Ruggeri both remain sidelined through injury, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka (thigh) and Johan Manzambi (calf) will need to be assessed ahead of kickoff.

Matty Cash is expected to miss this weekend’s game after picking up concussion on international duty with Poland, so Taylor Harwood-Bellis could continue at right-back where he made his full PL debut for Villa against Man United.

In a recent development, nicolas Jackson, John McGinn and Alysson were all on the scoresheet at Old Trafford and will hope to retain their starting spots in the final third. Leon Goretzka also scored against Man United but he faces competition from Joao Gomes to start in centre-midfield alongside Boubacar Kamara.

As for Sunderland, Le Bris has confirmed that captain Granit Xhaka (calf) and striker Brian Brobbey (thigh) are ruled out due to injury, joining Romaine Mundle (knee), Daniel Ballard and Habib Diarra (both thigh) in the treatment room.

However, Omar Alderete is back from a one-match suspension and could replace Luke O'Nein at centre-back, joining Trai Hume, Nordi Mukiele and Reinildo Mandava in defence.

Chemsdine Talbi was handed his first PL start of the season against Chelsea and will hope to continue on the left flank ahead of Nilson Angulo, while Wilson Isidor – who scored home and away against Villa last season – is set to lead the line in Brobbey's absence.

Sunderland possible starting lineup:.

Roefs; Hume, Mukiele, Alderete, Reinildo; Ahoka, Sadiki; Meunier, Le Fee, Talbi; Isidor.

Aston Villa's game management has become a growing concern, and Sunderland should fancy their chances of finding the net given that the hosts have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last six matches in all competitions.

While the Black Cats will be desperate to build on their victory over Chelsea as they bid to climb away from danger, the absence of both Xhaka and Brobbey is a real blow, and we expect Villa to ultimately navigate their way to a narrow triumph on home soil.

It has been revealed that michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he rolled out a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very swiftly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn.

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

It has been revealed that ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a significant game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

Industry observers note that on the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring problems to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

In a recent development, it now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

Sources indicate that that Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

In a recent development, united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

In a recent development, and then the red card which I thought was a really poor one. It’s difficult after that. Disappointed that with the chances we had we didn’t [get] more [out of the game].

It has been revealed that good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

It has been revealed that atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

It has been revealed that the one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

Manchester United fans have told Bryan Mbeumo to "go to bed" after the striker suggested he was playing GTA 6 ahead of Mauricio Pochettino first training session as manager.

A new era began at Man Utd on Wednesday with Pochettino's first day in charge, having flown in overnight following his final match as head coach of the USMNT.

Pochettino will take charge of first-team training for the first time on Thursday, with a daunting trip to Anfield to face Liverpool first up for the Argentine.

Full focus will be on making a positive start at the home of Man Utd's biggest rivals, but Mbeumo seemingly had something else top of his agenda on Wednesday evening.

A known video game fan, Mbeumo was one of thousands across the UK on Wednesday downloading the upcoming GTA game ahead of its midnight launch.

Mbeumo posted an image of him close to 12am set to play what many are calling one of the greatest video games of all time.

And it did not go down too well with some Man Utd fans online.

One fan wrote: "So we're sat in the relegation zone, got a must-win match against our biggest rivals at the weekend, latest gaffer's just flown in from America and bloody Mbeumo is up past midnight playing grand theft auto six.".

“Doing a GTA all nighter the day before his 1st training session with a new manager is definitely a choice,” read another post.

Another fan posted "you have training tomorrow go to bed lol", while a third added: "We’re 18th and we play Liverpool next.".

Ryan posted: "These lads have got to read the room and be a bit smarter with what they post.".

Grant Dalgleish added, with angry emojis: "He’s got training in the morning!!!!".

There is no suggestion for long, if at all, Mbeumo played the game ahead of Pochettino's first training session on Thursday morning.
