📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bournemouth and England star Alex Scott should set his sights ‘higher’ than Chelsea and aim to join ‘one of the biggest teams in Europe’ like Arsenal.

That’s according to Chris Waddle, who claims Scott has taken his game ‘to a new level’ over the last 18 months and is looking more and more like the ‘complete’ central midfielder.

Waddle’s comments come amid mounting speculation over Scott’s future, with Bournemouth bracing themselves for incoming offers to steal their prized possession away in the January transfer window.

Scott’s eye-catching breakthrough in the international arena has done little to quieten rumours that the 23-year-old could soon be destined for bigger and better things, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham all rumoured to be circling.

Though Scott is right now sidelined with a thigh injury, his stock continues to soar – and it’s understood the Cherries could be prepared to do business should they receive a bid in excess of £80m this winter.

In an interview with iGaming.com, ex-England international Waddle revealed how he had been keeping close tabs on Scott’s progress since he was first alerted to his potential at Bristol City.

In a recent development, ‘I’ve always liked Alex Scott. I think he’s a lovely, cultured player. There’s no doubt in my mind that in the last eighteen months, the kid’s taken his game to a fresh level,’ Waddle explained.

‘I followed him at Bristol City, and when he was there, I was speaking to someone that knew him who told me he was a Tottenham fan.

‘Tottenham have been collecting players in the last six months, but he is a top-class player and someone that would walk into any squad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

In a recent development, ‘Will they move for him? It seems unlikely given the midfielders they signed in the summer.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Chelsea are reportedly leading the hotly contested race to sign Scott and are said to be increasingly confident of reaching an agreement with Bournemouth for the central midfielder.

However, Waddle insists Scott should ideally be aiming higher than a move to Stamford Bridge, name-checking Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal as potential options.

‘According to reports, Chelsea retain the strongest interest in him. No disrespect to them, but I think he can look higher. I think he’s got the ability to play for the biggest teams in Europe: Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal,’ he added.

According to recent reports, ‘The guy looks like he’s a top player to me. He looks like he’s only going to get better. If I was a manager or a sporting director and I needed a midfielder, I would be looking at him.

‘He’s a complete midfielder. He can play as a 10, an 8, and a 6. He offers you a bit of everything. He reminds me a little bit of Rodri in the way that he likes to take the ball off the centre-back and start making things happen.

‘His composure and technique make him a standout player for any team looking to sign someone who can run a midfield and control the tempo.’.

While Bournemouth are in no hurry to part with Scott, the club’s hierarchy recognise that the England international may have ambitions to move on elsewhere near future.

For now, though, the Cherries are adamant that the Vitality Stadium remains the ‘right place’ for Scott.

‘At this point, we’re convinced that we’re the right place for Alex to be, for Alex to stay, and we’ll keep on addressing contract complications with Alex as we move through this year,’ Bournemouth owner Bill Foley told talkSPORT last month.

‘We’d love to have Alex stay here, sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul, and we’re still working on it. We haven’t given up.

‘But sometimes players get stars in their eyes and they think that Chelsea is the right place to go or Manchester City.’.

Scott’s current contract on the south coast runs through to June 2028.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.
  • The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:13.

In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.

The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.

Blackpool return to action on Saturday fresh off the dismissal of manager Evatt with the hopes of climbing away from the League One drop zone.

They endured a tough start to their first full campaign under Evatt, right now sitting 20th with just 12 points on the board from 13 games, winning three and losing seven of those.

The most recent of those victories came in October to end a six-game winless run in the third tier, but the Tangerines failed to build on it, going on to lose 4-1 to Mansfield and rescue a 1-1 draw against a Sheffield Wednesday side who played the second half with 10 men.

Then after scraping past non-league AFC Hornchurch in extra time in the FA Cup first round, they visited AFC Wimbledon last weekend and again came away empty-handed, having failed to find a leveller after Alistair Smith's 13th-minute.

That triggered the dismissal of Evatt by the club hierarchy on Thursday, and now under the temporary charge of Steve Thompson and only above the relegation zone on goal difference, they will be desperate to begin rebuilding confidence and a cushion over the bottom four with a much-needed home win.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to continue an upturn in form and their climb away from the relegation zone.

Wigan Athletic also endured a tough start to their League One campaign under Gary Caldwell, sitting bottom after 12 games with just seven points on the board having lost nine of those matches.

That was largely down to the Latics' struggles in attack, but they appear to have turned a corner since, winning two and drawing one of their last three league games while scoring five goals, firstly ending a three-game losing run by beating fellow strugglers Bromley 3-2.

Then following a stalemate with Mansfield Town and consecutive cup wins over Boreham Wood and Crewe Alexandra, Caldwell's men went into another important contest at home to Barnsley on Saturday and won 2-1 as Fraser Murray put them ahead, Cameron McGeehan pegged them back and Jensen Weir scored the decisive goal 15 minutes from time.

Still with plenty of cause for concern in their away record, having drawn one and lost six of seven league games on the road, but finally with some momentum on their side, Wigan Athletic head to Bloomfield Road in search of a third win in four games to build on their two-point lead over the drop zone.

Wigan Athletic League One form:.

Wigan Athletic form (all competitions):.

Blackpool were hit by a sickness bug for last weekend's game, with Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe among those to miss out.

They may be back in contention for Saturday, while defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe remain sidelined alongside George Honeyman.

Karoy Anderson will head back from international duty with Jamaica but was in action in Mexico on Wednesday, while Dion Charles, Jerry Yates, CJ Hamilton and Niall Ennis will all compete for attacking places after Dale Taylor and Tom Bloxham partnered up up top last time out.

Wigan Athletic will likely remain without forwards Dara Costelloe and Luke Harris due to ongoing injuries.

Scott Hogan is back in contention after a brief layoff and came off the bench last time out, but Caldwell may go unchanged from the Barnsley win, with Christian Saydee leading the line with support from Bradley Burrowes and Jon Mellish.

Murray will continue to offer attacking support in a wing-back role after his opener against Barnsley, while Weir and Max Power will continue in the middle of a 3-4-3 setup.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Southwood; Williams, Casey, Ashworth; Niskanen, Morgan, Brown, Coulson; Bowler, Charles, Yates.

Wigan Athletic possible starting lineup:.

Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett, Weir, Power, Murray; Burrowes, Mellish; Saydee.

Blackpool remain devoid of confidence and have been hit by injuries, illness and a managerial departure, but they still have more quality than their league standing suggests while the visitors have been poor away from home this season.

We see the Tangerines at least avoiding defeat against a resurgent Wigan team.

Beppe Marotta featured in the first episode of ‘L’impresa sportiva’, a segment on Il Sole 24 ORE’s TV program dedicated to the world of sport. He spoke about foreign ownership in Italy and the newly introduced stadium project, with his words via MilanPress.

“Football is a powerfully unifying phenomenon. After religion, I believe only sport can unite people by breaking down barriers. However, it’s also become a business. There are 12 foreign owners out of 20 in Serie A,” he began.

Pochettino arrived at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday and on Thursday took charge of his first training session. On Sunday comes his first game, away at Anfield against Liverpool.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be tasked with dragging Man Utd out of the relegation zone and back into the top echelons of English football.

The now-sacked Michael Carrick oversaw the club's worst start to a season in 40 years, and much of the malaise was put down to his tactical setups and a lack of energy from the players on the pitch.

And Pochettino, who is known for his hard drills in training, wants to bring the energy back to his players.

According to recent reports, “It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,” Pochettino told the club's official website.

Industry observers note that “Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

According to recent reports, “The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most vital thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

We need to love the players that we have, we need to support the players.

Sources indicate that “That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

“I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”.

On the significance of culture to success, he adds: “To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

“We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.”.

‘I thank Ancelotti for his confidence because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I’ve had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation.

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a message to Manchester United fans in his first interview as manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has replaced the sacked Michael Carrick, and flew in from the United States on Wednesday morning to begin his two-and-a-half-year contract.

Pochettino on Thursday oversaw his first training session as head coach, and has a quick turnaround before his first game in charge - which comes on Sunday at Anfield to face Liverpool.

The Argentine is aware he faces a baptism of fire at the home of a rival this weekend, and hopes to earn his connection with the fans by playing with "fight" and "for the win".

The fans need to see that we are going to fight ... and we are going to play for the win.

"I don't want to ask nothing because I think always we demand, demand, demand to the fans, but we need to provide to the fans before we demand," he told the club's official website.

Sources indicate that "I think we need to be the next to connect. We need to be the part that we create that energy that connect to the fans, to provide the fans.

"The fans need to see that we are going to fight, that we are Manchester United and we respect our history and we are going to play for the win. And for sure then our fans will be supporting us because what I hear and what I saw in the past, the supporters are amazing.".

According to recent reports, he continued: “I know very well what that game means and how key it is. The history talks for us and to what we need to expect.

“We need to make sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool youngster Trey Nyoni has picked out Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard as the ‘toughest opponent’ he has faced at the start of his career.

Odegaard has returned to his sparkling best this season, starting all ten of Arsenal’s opening matches in the Premier League with the reigning champions sitting five points clear at the summit.

Having managed just one goal across the Gunners’ title-winning campaign last term, the 27-year-old appears to have rediscovered his scoring boots, finding the net on five occasions in all competitions this term.

It was Odegaard’s 72nd-minute strike that proved the difference before the international break, when Mikel Arteta’s men were made to work for their victory at home to newly promoted Hull City.

The Norway international will no doubt be desperate to pick up where he left off when the north London giants return to top-flight against at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

Nyoni has himself enjoyed an impressive start to the season at Liverpool and locked horns with Odegaard when the pair did battle at Anfield at the start of the month.

And while Nyoni was taken off before the hour-mark on Merseyside, it’s clear Odegaard left a big impression on the 19-year-old in the 58 minutes his opposite number was on the pitch.

Asked to name the ‘toughest’ player he has come up against, Nyoni told The Inside Scoop, ‘For me personally, I would say Odegaard,’ as he looked back on that afternoon.

‘The way he plays, it’s very busy, moving around and always looking for an option.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s not easy as a midfielder. I think when you play against someone who is constantly moving, you know in the back of your mind that he could be here, but the next minute he’s there.’.

When asked if Odegaard perhaps doesn’t get the credit he deserves, Nyoni replied: ‘Yeah, I think the game is evolving and I think nowadays people look at No.10s and automatically think that if they’re not getting goals and assists, they’re not good.

Sources indicate that ‘For example, in our team we’ve got Flo [Wirtz]. I think Flo does a lot of stuff that people don’t really see.

‘I think what he brings to the team benefits the team. Just because he’s not scoring or assisting, doesn’t mean he’s not effective.

‘Nowadays, the idea that if a player isn’t getting goals or assists, they’re useless, but every player has their own role in the team.

‘Odegaard and people like Flo, if they’re not getting goals and assists, people that don’t watch the game automatically think they haven’t played well but that’s not how football works.’.

In the aftermath of Arsenal’s nervy win over Hull, club legend Paul Merson stated Odegaard had been ‘like a upcoming signing’ for Arteta this season.

‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it swiftly,’ Merson said of Odegaard on Sky Sports.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He moves it rapidly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance.

‘I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far.

It has been revealed that ‘Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show.’.

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

In a recent development, there was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

Industry observers note that so ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

Industry observers note that after weeks of searching, PEC Zwolle will have a upcoming face in the dugout for their upcoming clash against Telstar, with Alex Pastoor recently appointed as head coach until the end of the 2026-27 season. He replaces Henry van der Vegt, whose 15-month tenure ended in October.

Pastoor’s immediate task will be to build on his side’s four-game league unbeaten run, during which they have collected eight points from a possible 12, with only Heerenveen (12) and Ajax (10) boasting a better record in the division.

With three of their next four matches coming against teams currently in the top seven - AZ Alkmaar, Fortuna Sittard, and PSV Eindhoven - De Blauwvingers could use a win here as they look to put some distance between themselves and the drop zone before the end of 2026.

According to recent reports, both of Saturday’s opponents have managed just three clean sheets between them from 24 matches this season, so this weekend’s clash is likely to be decided at the attacking end. On that front, Zwolle have struggled compared to their hosts, scoring five fewer goals so far.

However, the visitors could tilt things in their favour with a quick start, and having scored the opener in four of the last five gameweeks, they may look to capitalise on a Telstar side that has conceded first four times during that span.

Jude Bellingham sealed England's stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain with a kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro as the couple made a rare public appearance together on Sunday.

England, who romped to a 3-0 lead with a superb display before the hour mark, were forced to weather a late onslaught from the Spanish after Elliot Anderson was shown a red card in the 63rd minute of the Nations League clash.

Although Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams managed to claw two back for this year's World Cup winners, England held on with a backs-to-the-wall effort in the closing stages, courtesy of a few fine saves from Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.

After England's victory, which called an end to Spain's historic 43-game unbeaten run, Bellingham was spotted celebrating with his model girlfriend Ashlyn inside the stadium.

Wearing a beaming smile, he went over to embrace both the 28-year-old American and his father Mark as the family soaked up the celebrations in the stands.

The Real Madrid superstar has largely kept his relationship with Ashlyn private since the pair were first linked in early 2025.

Jude Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashlyn Castro celebrate England's superb win over Spain.

The Real Madrid star then caught up with his dad Mark on a special night for the Bellinghams.

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California (@instagram/ashlyncastro).

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California who boasts over one million followers on Instagram, sharing fashion and beauty content online.

Spanish media waxed lyrical about Bellingham's display on the night, claiming he was 'determined to make a statement' at the stadium of Real Madrid's rivals Atletico.

Newspaper AS wrote: 'If anyone felt the match was crucial, it was Jude Bellingham. He stepped onto the Metropolitano pitch determined to make a statement, to impose his usual footballing and physical prowess.

'He exudes football in every movement, and his rise to the top is unstoppable.'.

It was a proud international break for the Bellinghams before a ball was kicked in Madrid, with Jude's 21-year-old younger brother Jobe also earning his first England call-up last week.

Jude and Jobe would have become the first brothers to play for England since Gary and Phil Neville 17 years ago, but the younger sibling stayed on Thomas Tuchel's bench as an unused substitute.

England, who topped Group C on goal difference over Spain, will now not play until the Nations League quarter-finals kick off next spring.

The final, should Tuchel's Three Lions make it that far, are scheduled for the summer.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Premier League board members have been given extra legal protection amid the threat of actions linked to the Manchester City case.

Eighteen clubs are reported to have supported changes to the league’s articles at a clubs meeting in central London on Thursday, which extend protections provided to individual board members to enable them to freely carry out their duties.

A 14-club majority is required for votes to be carried, and it was understood to have been comfortably above that.

The change comes after City sponsor Etihad stated in September it was considering legal action over the “damaging” implications of the independent commission’s guilty verdict against the club.

In a recent development, the airline was not named in the verdict, which found City had benefited from “sham” arrangements to inflate revenue and disguise costs to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules. City have appealed against the verdict. Another City sponsor, Etisalat, was reported by The Times to be considering similar action earlier this week.

The Press Association understands the issue was brought to a vote in order to bring the league’s individual legal cover in line with similar companies – including many of its clubs – and that these articles had not been looked at since the league’s inception in 1992.

There was no indication of any cap on the costs clubs could be exposed to as a result of the change to the league’s articles, and no wider discussion or questions raised on the City case despite this being the first shareholders’ meeting since the verdict was published on September 29.

Club executives also received a first enhancement of the season from referees’ chief Howard Webb.

He is understood to have accepted the 10th round of matches immediately before the November international break had been especially difficult.

Six on-field errors were identified by the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel which were not corrected by VAR intervention.

This is in part due to the high bar for intervention being operated this season, where referee’s on-field calls can only be overturned where it is felt the error was not a clear and obvious one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:39.

Mauricio Pochettino has explained the importance of 'creating the culture' at Manchester United, as the Argentine looks to build a positive environment following his arrival as head coach.

The 54-year-old will take charge of his first Man United match on Sunday afternoon, when the 20-time English champions tackle Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino officially started work as Red Devils head coach on Wednesday, having flown straight to England after managing his final USA game against Haiti.

The South American has taken charge of a team that currently sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up just eight points from their first 10 games of the season.

It has been revealed that “It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free," Pochettino told Man United's official website.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

It has been revealed that “Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

"When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero. I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.

“To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create. We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.

Sources indicate that “The best squad that we can have are the players that we have and we need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players.

"We need to provide all the tools for them to perform. It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the facility to translate all their talent on the field.”.

Pochettino's training session on Thursday included both Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu, with the defensive duo both in line to be available against Liverpool.

Paul Ince still cannot wrap his head around Manchester United’s decision to spend £50million on Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window.

Santos completed a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer, arriving alongside Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba as the Red Devils sought to bolster their depth in central midfield.

Santos enjoyed an encouraging pre-season, but started only four of United’s first ten Premier League matches under Michael Carrick before his sacking.

Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival may represent a fresh start for the £50m midfielder, but Ince believes United would have been better served spending that money elsewhere over the summer.

Industry observers note that ‘Why did they spend £50m on Santos?’ Ince told The Sun. ‘That’s £50m wasted. They could have put that into the defence or bought a striker.

‘They have [Kobbie] Mainoo, who needs to develop. He needs to be playing, not Santos.

‘Tielemans, again, fantastic at Villa but it’s a different conversation when you come to United.

It has been revealed that ‘Baleba didn’t play a lot last year. He comes in for £70m, plays a couple of games and he’s injured again.

‘The game’s changing. It’s not all pass, pass, pass now. You’ve got to win your duels. You used to hear Pep Guardiola say every time, “We didn’t win our duels, we didn’t win our tackles”.

But Ince fears that his former club will struggle to attract the world’s best talents given their current predicament.

Industry observers note that ‘What you’ve got is players playing for Manchester United, not Manchester United players,’ he added. ‘That’s a big difference.

In a recent development, ‘Who’s a Manchester United player out there? [Declan] Rice, Jude Bellingham. They are who you should be going for.

Eric Quill believes FC Dallas are a "well-oiled machine" going into the MLS Cup Playoffs and is excited to see what they can do in the first match of Round One against the Portland Timbers.

Dallas finished second in the Western Conference to ensure they had home advantage in the best-of-three series, having finished the regular season with just one loss in their last six games (W3 D2).

They recorded their best finish since 2016 when they topped the West, and they have qualified for the playoffs in back-to-back seasons, though they were knocked out in Round One last year.

Quill is confident Dallas can improve on that result, though, claiming the drop in temperatures will only play into his team's strength on the press.

"We are a well-oiled machine right now, as far as across the board, just guys, how bought in they are and how much they're up for this," Quill told MLSSoccer.com.

"And our team speed, our pressing ability, the change of weather going into the high 60s, low 70s, is only going to help our game model, because we want to press and be really proactive, front-footed.

"We're going to be on people from minute 1 to 95.".

Portland, meanwhile, just snuck into the automatic playoff spots due to a strong finish to the regular season.

They went unbeaten in their last five games, winning each of the last four (D1), including a 2-0 win over Austin FC on Decision Day, which meant they pipped the Seattle Sounders to seventh.

"When we look at the progress, there have been some improvements, but you need to be consistent in that," head coach Marti Cifuentes mentioned.

"We have to learn to be ourselves, whatever the game scenario. If we start well, then we need to keep on our philosophy.

Sources indicate that "But obviously there is an opposition as well. There is always an opponent that prepares well for the game, and that's why the game is so beautiful, because sometimes you just need to cope with the reality of the game.

"I would say we need to at our best in our key identity and principles of the game.".

Joaquin Valiente got the scoring started for Dallas in their win over the Rapids on Decision Day, netting just his third goal of the season.

He has been an effective playmaker, though, with nobody on the team bettering his 13 assists, while he also topped the charts for crosses (115) and chances created (48).

Jimer Fory has helped keep the Timbers ticking throughout the season, with no Portland player registering more touches (2,016), interceptions (63) or possessions won (161).

Only Finn Surman (1,570) attempted more passes than the Colombian (1,437), but Fory was a solid presence at the back with more successful tackles (32/54) than anyone else.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Industry observers note that thomas Tuchel had remarked he wanted evidence.
  • Recent findings suggest that he needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

Industry observers note that thomas Tuchel had remarked he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Recent findings suggest that he needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’.

Something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller.

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback.

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead.

Recent findings suggest that yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

In a recent development, spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

It has been revealed that england had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

In a recent development, england ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

It has been revealed that spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

In a recent development, spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

Pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

England got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move.

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot.

According to recent reports, the referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

Recent findings suggest that there were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

According to recent reports, eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

It has been revealed that four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Sources indicate that kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded.

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net.

In a recent development, but then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

The atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi is targeting a move outside of the Premier League despite interest from Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham, according to reports.

Kroupi joined Bournemouth in a £12 million deal from French side Lorient last year and scored 13 goals in his first season in the Premier League.

The 20-year-old has suffered a disrupted start to the new campaign as he required surgery on a foot injury sustained during a pre-season training session in Austria in July.

Kroupi returned in Bournemouth’s 3-0 win away to Manchester United on October 25 and has made three more appearances as a substitute for Marco Rose’s side.

During the international break, Kroupi was handed his senior debut for France as he featured in the 3-1 defeat to Italy, as well as in the 2-1 win over Turkey.

The French striker has attracted interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham, while Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Barcelona have also been monitoring his progress in the Premier League.

However, David Ornstein has claimed that Kroupi will look to move overseas when he leaves Bournemouth, although the club are not looking to sell the forward in the January transfer window.

‘There was a substantial story recently about Alex Scott possibly leaving in the January transfer window, that was conditional on Bournemouth receiving £100 million and being in a really strong position in the Premier League where that becomes a bit of a no-brainer because in six months’ time he’ll have a year to go on his contract and it’s a very different conversation,’ Ornstein mentioned on The Athletic FC’s podcast.

‘Kroupi has got much longer on his contract for a start, so there’s no massive need to sell in a way you would consider selling Scott.

‘He’s been out injured for longer as well, so I think Bournemouth want to make use of him this season and they don’t think their chances of recouping significant value in the summer will be much worse than in January, probably better actually.

‘My information around Kroupi is he would like to move at some point, outside of England.

According to recent reports, ‘You’ve seen very heavy reporting around PSG and Barcelona. If he continues to show the level of form that he was displaying prior to his injury, the biggest clubs in world football want him.

‘It’s no surprise he’s high up on Premier League club recruitment lists, but if what I’m hearing to date is anything to go by, those Premier League clubs may be disappointed because he could be travelling back to warmer climes.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have been left red-faced after a drone covertly filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session and posted the footage to YouTube.

The Argentine, who signed up to replace Michael Carrick as United’s head coach last week, arrived at Carrington on Wednesday to start work with his upcoming club.

With United languishing in the drop zone, Pochettino faces a brutal opening fixture of his reign, away at Liverpool.

But his preparations for that match have already been compromised in a concerning security breach at United’s training centre, after a drone secretly recorded 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first session with the club, with footage posted on YouTube for all to see.

The drone does not appear to have entered Carrington’s airspace at any point, but footage filmed with a zoom lens highlights the session in clear detail.

The YouTube channel which posted the clip followed it up with a statement claiming they had broken no laws by recording the session as the airspace around Carrington is unrestricted.

It has been revealed that no players or staff caught in the footage appeared to be aware of the fact they were being filmed. At the time of writing, the clip has accrued over 40,000 views.

The footage reveals the United squad working in two groups. One was being put through a rondo on one pitch, while Pochettino led the other through what appeared to be a tactical session on another. Both groups appeared to comprise a blend of first-team and academy players.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Standard Sport.

Fulham are reportedly working to extend Calvin Bassey's contract amid interest from Manchester United.

The Red Devils are expected to bring a centre-back to Old Trafford in the January transfer window due to their problems in that area of the field.

Man United are planning to overhaul their defensive unit next summer, as Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are all out of contract, while there is speculation surrounding the futures of Matthijs de Ligt, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

However, due to the team's severe defensive problems this term, it is likely that a latest centre-back will be targeted when the winter window opens for business.

Man United have conceded 19 times in their 10 Premier League matches this season, which is the joint-third worst record in the division.

The Red Devils have actually not kept a single clean sheet in the Premier League this term, while they have also conceded eight times in their four Champions League matches.

Bassey has allegedly been identified by Man United as a leading target, with the 26-year-old's contract due to expire at the end of the campaign.

Fulham do have the option to activate another year on the Nigeria international's deal, but the club are looking to sign him to a long-term contract.

According to The Athletic, Fulham are at the moment pushing to extend his deal, with the London team having no intention of letting him leave in the winter market.

Bassey has captained Fulham this season, making 12 appearances in 2026-27, while he has represented the club on 113 occasions in all competitions.

The defender has also played for Rangers and Ajax during his professional career.

Bassey gained Champions League experience during his time at Ajax, while he has now played 104 times in the Premier League for Fulham, scoring three goals and registering one assist.

New Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed with funds during the January transfer window.

Arsenal and Liverpool have both been linked with the England international and although Hasselbaink is a keen admirer of the 23-year-old, he feels his old club would be better suited by targeting the Gunners’ out of favour Spain international Martin Zubimendi.

The World Cup winner is yet to start a Premier League game this season amid increased competition as a result of Bruno Guimaraes’ arrival from Newcastle.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino believes it is a "mistake" to solely focus on Manchester United's current predicament, and vows to "change things" at the club.

Pochettino began his tenure as United boss on Wednesday, leaving his position as United States head coach after signing off with a win in the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals against Haiti.

He is tasked with improving United's current position, with the team sitting 18th in the Premier League table after the first 10 games.

The Red Devils have won just one of their first 10 matches in the league (D5 L4), while they are winless in eight Premier League matches for just the second time, also doing so in April/May 2025.

By the time United kick off against Liverpool in Pochettino's first game in charge, they will have been in the drop zone for 15 consecutive days – their longest run of days in the top-flight drop zone since September/October 1986 (28 days).

But Pochettino does not want to focus on the negatives, instead choosing to be optimistic about what United could do.

"It's a mistake to see the situation," Pochettino told United's social channels. "We need to see the potential of this club.

"It's about to start to act and to change things, and to try to affect, in a good way, all the areas, to try to really believe that we can recover that feeling about to win.

"The most crucial thing is for us to start to work hard to recover that feeling. That feeling is about being winners, to win games, to perform. But that is not only to talk about winning.".

The importance of Sunday's fixture isn't lost on Mauricio.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 19, 2026.

Reports suggest Pochettino will have a say in whatever business United do in the January transfer window, but he has over a month until he can add reinforcements to his squad.

United have 10 games to play before the end of the calendar year, and the Argentinian is determined to get the best out of his current crop of players.

"The best request that we can have, the players that we have, and we need to love the players that we have," Pochettino added.

"We need to support the players; we need to provide all the tools for their performance.

"It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the possibility to translate all their talent on the field.".

Pochettino will be the first-ever United manager to see his first league game come against rivals, Liverpool.

Just one of the Red Devils' last nine managers (incl. caretakers) has lost his first Premier League game of a spell in charge of the club (W4 D4), with Erik ten Hag losing 1-2 to Brighton in August 2022.

Though Liverpool are the favourites to win – with the Opta supercomputer giving them a 57.3% chance of victory on Sunday – Pochettino has his eyes on three points.

"We are going to go there, to Anfield, with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United," he said.

"We need to make sure that we are brave, and we are protagonists, and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester City could lose an experienced midfielder on a free transfer at the end of the season, with fresh reports suggesting that the player has already identified the European leagues in which he would prefer to continue his career.
  • Mateo Kovacic is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium when his contract expires in June 2027, according to transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, who has also provided an patch on the Croatia international's preferred destinations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 20:47.

Manchester City could lose an experienced midfielder on a free transfer at the end of the season, with fresh reports suggesting that the player has already identified the European leagues in which he would prefer to continue his career.

Mateo Kovacic is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium when his contract expires in June 2027, according to transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, who has also provided an patch on the Croatia international's preferred destinations.

Speaking to Marca, Moretto claimed that the 32-year-old would welcome a return to Spain or Italy, where he previously represented Real Madrid and Inter Milan respectively.

"He will leave City at the end of the season," Moretto remarked, before explaining that Kovacic "would like to return to Spain or Italy", although his salary expectations could influence his options.

The update comes as Kovacic struggles to secure regular playing time under Enzo Maresca, having fallen down the midfield pecking order since the Italian replaced Pep Guardiola.

While City have not officially declared his departure, the midfielder is approaching the final seven months of his contract without a reported agreement over an extension.

Kovacic joined Manchester City from Chelsea in June 2023, signing a four-year contract in a deal worth an initial £25m, with a further £5m potentially payable in add-ons.

The Croatia international was recruited to provide experience, technical quality and composure in midfield, having previously enjoyed considerable success with both Real Madrid and Chelsea.

However, injuries have increasingly disrupted his time in Manchester.

The midfielder was restricted to just nine appearances during the 2025-26 campaign after undergoing surgery to address a troublesome heel problem.

Although he has returned to action this season, his opportunities have remained limited under Maresca.

Kovacic has made eight appearances across all competitions, contributing one goal and one assist, but only one of those outings has been a Premier League start.

He has also been used sparingly in the Champions League, with the manager preferring other midfield options for the majority of City's European fixtures.

His two full appearances in the EFL Cup underline the change in his status, although he was entrusted with the captain's armband in one of those matches.

The situation represents a considerable shift for a player who has won four Champions League titles and previously played an important role in some of Europe's most successful teams.

Reports linking Kovacic with an exit have circulated for several months.

In September, the Croatian was reportedly considering a January departure after becoming frustrated with his lack of opportunities.

Moretto's latest information, however, points towards a summer move when Kovacic would become available without a transfer fee.

From January, the midfielder will be eligible to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with clubs outside England, potentially allowing him to arrange his next destination before the end of the campaign.

Kovacic's reported preference for Spain or Italy would represent a return to familiar surroundings rather than an entirely latest challenge.

The midfielder spent two seasons with Inter Milan before joining Real Madrid in 2015, where he won three consecutive Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018.

He subsequently moved to Chelsea, initially on loan, and spent five seasons at Stamford Bridge before completing his switch to City.

His experience in Serie A has already attracted attention from Italian clubs.

Juventus were linked with a move for Kovacic in September, when reports suggested that the Turin giants had identified him as one of several potential free-agent signings for the summer of 2027.

The Bianconeri were also mentioned to be monitoring Fikayo Tomori and David Raum as part of their efforts to strengthen the squad without paying substantial transfer fees.

AC Milan have separately been mentioned among Kovacic's possible suitors, although there is no indication that either Italian club has reached an agreement with the player.

The possibility of returning to La Liga also remains open, but Moretto's comments did not identify a Spanish club currently negotiating for his signature.

His wages could prove the biggest obstacle to a move.

Despite the prospect of securing an accomplished international without paying City a transfer fee, interested clubs would still need to reach an agreement over a salary package acceptable to Kovacic.

For City, the latest update raises the prospect of losing another member of Guardiola's former midfield without receiving a transfer fee.

Maresca's current selection decisions suggest that Kovacic is no longer regarded as an automatic starter, although the Croatian remains part of the squad and has not publicly confirmed any prepares to leave.

With his contract due to expire next June, the coming months could determine whether he completes his final season in Manchester or attracts an offer to bring forward his departure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England will learn their opponents for the Nations League quarter-finals on Friday morning.

The Three Lions beat Spain in dramatic circumstances in Madrid to top their group last week, and can now avoid the likes of France, Germany and Portugal in the quarter-finals as a result.

But the draw might still throw up some tricky fixtures as England look to improve on their best-ever finish in this competition, which came when they crossed the line in third in 2019.

Here is all you need to know about their potential opponents...

England are in Pot 1 for the Nations League draw, along with France, Germany and Portugal.

The teams in Pot 2 are Belgium, Spain, the Netherlands and Norway.

The Nations League draw will pit each of the four teams in Pot 1 against one of those in Pot 2, for a two-legged quarter-final.

According to recent reports, there is one provision, though: teams from the same group cannot be drawn against each other, meaning England cannot face Spain at this stage of the competition. They could, however, come across them in the semi-finals or final.

As such, England could draw Belgium, the Netherlands, or Norway in the quarter-final.

Semi-final matchups will be determined by another draw following the quarter-finals.

England’s dream opponent at this stage of the Nations League is Norway.

FIFA sees Martin Odegaard and Erling Haaland’s side as comfortably the lowest-ranked of England’s three potential opponents.

That is in spite of their impressive World Cup campaign - where they were knocked out in the quarter-finals by England - and the fact they turned over both Denmark and Wales in the November international break.

England’s nightmare draw, meanwhile, would see them pitted against Belgium.

It is tough to say whether Belgium or the Netherlands would be the tougher opponent at this stage - FIFA ranks them at eighth and ninth in the world, respectively - but the Red Devils just pip their neighbours.

They finished second in their group, just a single point off winners France. A pair of one-sided victories over Turkiye and Italy got them to this stage.

The quarter-final first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The semi-finals and final will be played in June 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frank Lampard appears to have endorsed Chelsea’s pursuit of Alex Scott while revealing his ‘love’ for the ‘quality’ Bournemouth and England midfielder.

Scott has established himself as one of the most sought-after central midfielders in English football having joined Bournemouth from Bristol City back in 2023.

With attentions beginning to turn towards the January transfer window, speculation is mounting that the 23-year-old could have his head turned amid strong interest from the Premier League’s elite.

Though he picked up a thigh injury while on international duty with England last month, Scott’s outstanding performance in the Three Lions’ thumping 7-0 win over Croatia did little to quieten rumours of a potential big-money move.

Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham have all been credited with an interest in recent weeks and months, but Chelsea reportedly find themselves in pole position to land Scott this winter.

The Blues are actively scouring the market for midfield reinforcements after failing to bring in a replacement for Enzo Fernandez in the summer and are said to be ‘increasingly confident’ of reaching an agreement for Scott.

Up until this point, Bournemouth have publicly played down speculation that Scott could be on the move, especially midway through the campaign when they risk derailing the side’s encouraging progress under Marco Rose.

However, it’s understood an offer in region of £100million could be enough to convince the Cherries into selling Scott in what would undoubtedly be one of this January’s biggest deals.

One man who knows more than anyone what it takes to thrive in Chelsea’s midfield is Lampard, arguably the club’s greatest ever player, who won 14 trophies across an illustrious 13-year career at Stamford Bridge.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

During a wide-ranging interview on the Rio Ferdinand Presents YouTube channel, Lampard made it clear just how highly he rated Scott when he was asked to name his dream Premier League midfield three on current form.

‘I don’t want to leave anyone out because there are some teams that are doing some stuff… I’m loving what Brighton are doing at the moment but you do come back to the bigger players sometimes, maybe Cole Palmer or Rayan Cherki,’ the Coventry head coach told Ferdinand.

‘I love Alex Scott at Bournemouth, I think he’s quality.

‘He’s injured now for a short period but I think he’s real quality in that modern all-rounder [role], in the double six/eight.’.

Revealing other candidates for his midfield three, Lampard added: ‘I’ve got to put Elliot Anderson in there, in my opinion, for the way he’s playing.

‘I’m trying to think of the attacking options… I think I’d put Anderson and Declan Rice as the two sixes and then I’ll go for an eight/ten.

‘I’m trying to think of the eight-ten that’s really being decisive at the minute. Rayan Cherki is doing bits, I love Cole Palmer.’.

Lampard went on to express his admiration for Martin Odegaard, explaining how he had shut down one of his close friends who had been criticising the Arsenal captain.

It has been revealed that ‘I really like Martin Odegaard. A mate of mine, an Arsenal fan, doesn’t like Odegaard, he gets on my nerves! He’s a good player,’ he went on.

‘He [Odegaard] brilliant. I bumped into him with my son as well recently, him and Kai Havertz, I know Kai, at a hotel, my boy was buzzing and they were so lovely with my boy, not that that makes them good players.

Sources indicate that ‘They were brilliant, the pair of them. And I remarked to my son, “This boy [Odegaard] is a good player”, because you see all sides of the game, especially when you do my job and you watch him press and what he does for the team.’.

Lampard also praised Odegaard’s midfield partner Rice and questioned the ‘harsh’ criticism the England international has at times received during his career.

‘I do love Declan Rice and I think he’s become a conversation point because when you get to be so good and compete at such a level, people try to pick holes in your game and I think it’s harsh,’ he continued.

‘I think he’s a really good player and it’s just a common thing that comes with the territory.

‘It’s fine and Declan will just shrug it off.’.

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 21:00, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 21:44.

Eyeing up a place in the top four of the Premier League, in-form Bournemouth welcome Nottingham Forest to the Vitality Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The spoils were shared in the last meeting between these two teams in May, with an opener from Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White cancelled out in the second half by Cherries attacker Marcus Tavernier to rescue a 1-1 draw.

Bournemouth’s 2026-27 campaign started with just two wins in eight matches across all competitions (D3 L3), including no wins in six Premier League fixtures, but the Cherries have since put together an impressive eight-game winning streak under new boss Marco Rose.

A slender 2-1 success at Ipswich Town prior to the international break helped them climb up to seventh in the table, just three points behind Liverpool in fourth, and they are now aiming to win five straight top-flight games for the first time in their history.

Since the start of October, Bournemouth have scored more goals across all competitions than any other Premier League team (22), netting at least two goals in each game during their eight-match winning run.

In-form striker Evanilson has been Bournemouth's driving force, with the Brazilian’s goal against Ipswich making him the first Cherries player to score in five successive PL matches. He also has the joint-most top-flight goal involvements this season (nine - five goals, four assists), level with Erling Haaland (nine goals).

Not only do Bournemouth enter Saturday’s contest having never lost in eight previous Premier League battles with Nottingham Forest (W4 D4), but Rose has also won his last four meetings with teams managed by Oliver Glasner (all in the Bundesliga between 2021 and 2023).

After enduring a sluggish start to life under Glasner, winning just one of their first nine Premier League games, Nottingham Forest entered the international break on a massive high after securing a statement 3-1 victory over Manchester City at the City Ground – their first home league win of the campaign.

Liam Delap ended a five-game goal drought with a superb brace against his former club that followed an earlier opener from Jair Cunha, with Forest scoring more goals in this match (three) than they had in their previous six home league fixtures combined (two).

Sitting 16th in the Premier League table and one point above the drop zone, Forest must now translate that momentum onto their travels, having failed to keep an away clean sheet in the top flight since April while losing their last two games on the road against Crystal Palace (3-1) and Brentford (2-0).

Although Forest have scored the second-fewest goals in the division this term (nine), Glasner – who takes charge of his 100th Premier League match on Saturday – will hope that his team’s clinical display against Man City signals a turning point after weeks of frustration in front of goal.

The Tricky Trees head to the Vitality Stadium seeking to win back-to-back league games for only the second time this calendar year, but they are winless in six away league encounters against Bournemouth (D2 L4).

Eli Junior Kroupi is another attacking option pushing to start having made a full recovery from injury and scoring his first goal for France last weekend, while in-demand midfielder Alex Scott is available to start for the first time since suffering a thigh injury with England in October.

As for Nottingham Forest, Nicolas Dominguez (hamstring) remains a long-term absentee and has been joined in the treatment room by Callum Hudson-Odoi (groin), while Neco Williams (ankle) and Xaver Schlager (thigh) have both emerged as doubts after picking up injuries with Wales and Austria respectably over the international break.

Delap is bidding to score in successive PL games for the first time since April 2025 with Ipswich and is expected to lead the line once again, with Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye potentially providing support in advanced positions; the latter’s inclusion would allow James McAtee to move back into a deeper midfield position.

Although six of Forest's last seven Premier League away games have seen both teams score, we are backing the Cherries to frustrate an opponent they have historically enjoyed facing and secure three more points without reply to extend their impressive winning run to nine matches.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo will sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

The presence of Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass in the group rather debunks this, though, given neither has started a Premier League match this season.

Predicted Man Utd XI vs Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo.

Wes Brown believes Manchester United should still be aiming for a top-five finish this season after Mauricio Pochettino was appointed head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has officially taken the reins at Old Trafford after his final two matches with the United States national team.

Pochettino has undoubtedly been thrown in at the deep end, with United winless in their last eight Premier League matches and facing Liverpool in his first game on Sunday.

But former Red Devils defender Brown believes that the Argentine has the quality to inspire a quick turnaround from his latest crop of players.

Sources indicate that ‘Poch is very experienced, and he has his own style of play, but it’s all about consistency, he told Metro. ‘Making the players believe they’re good enough and making sure they do it week in, week out.

‘We’ve had no momentum; we’ve played well here and there in games, and when we did we managed to score, but at the same time we’ve been very poor at times and open to teams scoring at will, making loads of mistakes.

‘The confidence isn’t there, but he’ll be coming in and just trying to get consistency through the team.

‘When a new manager comes in, the players really make an effort, that’s just the way it goes, but then it’s up to the manager to keep that going through the season, and whether or not he’ll be able to, we’ll all have to see.’.

Pochettino brings with him extensive experience in the Premier League but also a proven track record of nurturing young talent into the first team.

#1900. Tech Report: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease

Tech Report: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 94 min read (18848 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~94 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2.
  • According to recent reports, alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an age-associated neurodegenerative disease affecting millions worldwide, with a prevalence of roughly 10–30% among individuals older than 65 years3.
  • The hypothalamus, a small but complex brain region, orchestrates a wide range of physiological and neuroendocrine processes frequently dysregulated in ageing and AD2,7.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2. These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with AD and age-matched non-dementia control participants. We show that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, showing notable changes in both volumes and gene expression during ageing and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. These signatures were reflected in specific cell types: microglia transitioned to a pro-inflammatory state, whereas inhibitory neurons within sleep-regulating and circadian-regulating hypothalamic subregions showed the most profound transcriptional alterations, including disruptions in ligand–receptor interactions and G-protein-coupled receptor signalling. HypoAD provides a high-resolution volumetric map and a transcriptomic atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, relating lifestyle and behavioural changes to the relevant volumetric and molecular pathways. In addition, HypoAD provides a framework to investigate hypothalamic dysfunction and establishes a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating physiological disruptions to potentially slow disease progression.

According to recent reports, alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an age-associated neurodegenerative disease affecting millions worldwide, with a prevalence of roughly 10–30% among individuals older than 65 years3. Although its cardinal feature is cognitive impairment, AD manifests as a systemic condition involving profound disruptions in sleep, circadian rhythms, metabolic homeostasis, stress responses and neuroendocrine functions1. The canonical neuropathological hallmarks are extracellular amyloid-β plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), which alongside widespread neuroinflammation and volumetric brain changes, also intensify with ageing1,4. Because cognitive decline has traditionally guided both diagnosis and research, investigation has focused mainly on the hippocampus and cortex5. As the effects of AD on other brain regions remain poorly understood, investigating these understudied areas is crucial for elucidating the full spectrum of disease mechanisms and developing new therapeutics6.

The hypothalamus, a small but complex brain region, orchestrates a wide range of physiological and neuroendocrine processes frequently dysregulated in ageing and AD2,7. Emerging evidence suggests that hypothalamic dysfunction not only correlates with but also actively exacerbates AD pathology and cognitive decline1. Specifically, pathology within hypothalamic subregions, such as the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN)8, arcuate nucleus (ARC)1,9 and mammillary body10, has been associated with prominent sleep disturbances, metabolic dysfunction and memory deficits observed in patients with AD. These systemic disruptions, in turn, are proposed to create a vicious cycle that further accelerates disease progression and cognitive decline1.

It has been revealed that despite its central role in homeostasis and brain ageing2,11, the hypothalamus remains an understudied region in the context of human ageing and AD. In particular, we have a limited understanding of the volumetric, cellular and molecular changes within the human hypothalamus during these processes. Although studies in animal models have highlighted hypothalamic involvement in ageing and neurodegeneration2,11,12, human studies remain scarce. This may be in part because the hypothalamus is more evolutionarily conserved than the cortex and is critical for survival, and thus it may show less overt vulnerability to ageing and prevalent diseases13. This paucity is especially pronounced for investigations that combine high-resolution imaging with single-cell analyses, complementary approaches essential for dissecting the anatomical and cellular heterogeneity of this complex brain region. This knowledge gap hinders our ability to determine how specific hypothalamic subregions and cell populations contribute to ageing and AD, and why they show differential vulnerability.

Sources indicate that here we present HypoAD, a multimodal atlas combining two powerful, cross-scale approaches. First, we performed high-resolution volumetric analysis of clinical imaging data from 458 individuals across the adult lifespan with varying cognitive and amyloid-β pathological statuses. Second, we generated a complementary single-cell transcriptomic atlas, comprising 614,403 nuclei from the hypothalami of 17 post-mortem donors, including young and older individuals with or without clinical and neuropathological diagnoses of AD, in which sampling was specifically enriched for the SCN, ARC and mammillary body. This dual-modality approach reveals the subregion-specific and cell-type-specific alterations of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD.

In a recent development, neuroimaging studies have reported changes in hypothalamic volumes associated with ageing and cognitive decline14. Previous analyses were low-resolution or limited to major areas, masking disease-relevant subregions such as the ARC and SCN14. To overcome this limitation, we leveraged a newly developed volumetric atlas of the human hypothalamus15 to delineate and measure 13 hypothalamic and 12 extrahypothalamic structures (Supplementary Table 1). Our analysis included a clinical imaging dataset of 458 individuals across two previously described cohorts: the Adult Metabolism & Brain Resilience (AMBR) study16 (n = 202) and the Connectomics in Brain Aging and Dementia (CBA) study17 (n = 256) (Extended Data Fig. 1a).

Pearson correlation analysis revealed that whereas total hypothalamic volume indicated a weak correlation with age (r = 0.15, adjusted P = 1.5 × 10 −3, Fig. 1a, Supplementary Table 2), its constituent subregions showed stronger age-related correlations. Specifically, the lateral hypothalamus volume was negatively correlated with age (r = −0.22, adjusted P = 5.2 × 10−6), suggesting age-related atrophy. By contrast, the volumes of the SCN (r = 0.26, adjusted P = 2.8 × 10−8), ARC (r = 0.32, adjusted P = 1.7 × 10−11), paraventricular nucleus (r = 0.35, adjusted P = 6.9 × 10−14), periventricular nucleus (r = 0.34, adjusted P = 8.8 × 10−13) and dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus (DMH) (r = 0.23, adjusted P = 1.8 × 10−6) all increased with age across all 458 individuals in two studies: AMBR and CBA (Fig. 1a,b and Supplementary Tables 2 and 3). A few subregions (SCN, mammillary body, dorsal periventricular nucleus and tuberomammillary nucleus) showed lower test–retest reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) < 0.4; Extended Data Fig. 1b), probably reflecting their small size and limited tissue contrast; volumetric results for these subregions should therefore be interpreted with caution. In the AMBR cohort the positive correlation between DMH volume and age was not detected in cognitively normal, amyloid-β negative individuals (Extended Data Fig. 1c,d and Supplementary Tables 2 and 3), but it remained present in the larger harmonized two-study cohort (n = 458; Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). To test whether this age-related increase in DMH volume itself differs by disease status, an age × group interaction model (group: cognitively normal and amyloid-negative versus all others; Methods) showed no significant interaction (effect size/estimate ± standard error (s.e.) = −0.041 ± 0.025, adjusted P = 0.12, Supplementary Table 4), indicating that age-related increase in DMH volume does not differ significantly between groups. This suggests that the DM–age association probably reflects a general feature of hypothalamic ageing in this subregion—which is implicated in sleep–wakefulness18 and body-weight regulation19—rather than a process specific to neurodegeneration.
